newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danmark's BG Bank gets government boost.
newsitem.headline: Danmark's BG Bank gets government boost.

text.p: Denmark's third-largest bank, BG Bank, is to get 4,000 new customers from January 1 when local authority-backed home help firms must open accounts with BG on government orders, the daily Berlingske Tidende said on Friday.

Key to the new trade ministry regulation is that BG, formed a year ago from a merger of the post office Girobank and Bikuben savings bank, is the only bank using a giro payment system in which users can fill in payment blanks by hand.
The ministry favours this for an industry where most of the firms are small businesses employing unskilled labour, where invoices are written out by the worker in the client's home.

Danish Bankers' Association vice-chairman Peter Straarup, a director of rival Den Danske Bank, said the order gave BG an unacceptable advantage and he would seek a way in which all banks could meet the terms of the trade industry's directive.
Denmark's generous social service system provides local authority subsidies of over 50 percent for companies providing cleaning, shopping and other domestic services for ratepayers.

The aim is to eradicate the black economy by making home help available at similar prices to those offered by unregistered workers who charge less but pay no tax. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
